At Physical Intelligence, we believe that general purpose models that can control any robot to perform any task will be the future of robotic control.

A few months ago we announced π0, our first general-purpose robotic foundation model that could be fine-tuned to a diverse range of tasks (folding laundry, cleaning a table, scooping coffee beans, etc) and that could control a variety of different robot type (robots with two arms, single-arm platforms, mobile robots, etc). Today, we are releasing the code and weights for the π0 as part of our experimental openpi repository.

snippets: What Physical Intelligence has actually demonstrated with π0.5, what stays a company claim, and why the open weights lag the flagship. ... Physical Intelligence is a robotics lab whose π0.5 model is the open reference point for generalist robot policies. Its best-documented result, arXiv 2504.16054, shows π0.5 cleaning kitchens and bedrooms in unseen homes, with real-world success self-reported. The openpi code is Apache 2.0, π0.5 base weights arrived in September 2025, and no later model has open weights.

The original release covered π0 base weights and code, fine-tuned ALOHA and DROID checkpoints, inference examples, and fine-tuning code. π0.5 weights came later: the README records "[Sept 2025] We released pi05, an upgraded version of pi0 with better open-world generalization," with a base checkpoint at gs://openpi-assets/checkpoints/pi05_base.

pi05_base checkpoint on Hugging Face - the base weights added in September 2025, downloadable and checkable against the LIBERO scores. Apache License 2.0 - the licence that covers the openpi code, and only the code. LIBERO benchmark - the definition of the Spatial 98.8, Object 98.2, Goal 98.0 and Libero-10 92.4 suites. DROID dataset - one of the two fine-tuned checkpoint targets in the original openpi release.
